rows.skeptic: Refuted. The proposed closure never puts the requirement's own check on a default path. That check is 'a central component ingests cell reports and re-issues capital envelopes; removing ingestion leaves envelopes un-renewed'. The only production caller of Platform::ingest_cell_report (platform.rs:7419, not :7351) is qip-api/src/mesh.rs:1749. MeshSettings::from_env (mesh.rs:149) returns None unless QIP_MESH_CELLS is set. The code cannot default it: each cell entry must be 'cell=host:port', and the parse error says 'the address is the cell's identity on this transport, so it cannot be left to a default'. The variable is also unset on purpose. infrastructure/terraform/catalogue.tf says Cloud Run publishes exactly one port and that the real centre-to-node path is the Pub/Sub control fabric (ADR 0024 work, §46.1). qip-acceptance/tests/manifest_wiring.rs::the_centre_declares_no_mesh_listener_because_cloud_run_publishes_one_port enforces this. So putting ingestion on a default path needs one of two things. Option one is a deployed mesh or Pub/Sub fabric, which means infra and billing, and editing infrastructure/environments/** is protected. Option two is a new ADR for a different cell-report transport on the API's single port. Wiring the market factory into qip-api by default would also reverse a fail-closed default. qip-deepbrain/src/breadth.rs says unset means 'no breadth at all … the fail-closed default, because each section commits the platform to something'. A qip-api test that configures the mesh explicitly does not prove a default path under bar part 2. The row's gap also names 'deployment'. Second-best bucket: DECIDE_ADR (new transport). The separate service is only a flag: the strategic rows run inside the same run_cycle. The only blocker is owner decision O24, whether to split the strategic lattice into its own service. That is a product decision the 2026-10-31 delegation now hands to the orchestrator. The audit-5 bar (part 2) counts a shipped binary's default path even when it is not deployed, so the split can be built without new billed Cloud Run instances. Deploying it later is the billed part.
rows.closure: Write a new ADR deciding O24 conservatively: run the weeks-months and quarters-years rows in a separate shipped process (a new apps binary or a qip-deepbrain mode, not deployed or costed until the owner funds it), and have the kernel read its forecasts and backlog questions while it is down. Add an integration test that kills that process and asserts execution cycles still pass and the backlog grows.
